sections.name: AnalyticsController
sections.title: Analytics routes
sections.what: Defines five routes under the analytics address: dashboard, trends, adherence, water intake and risk score. Each reads the signed-in user and returns its result inside a data field. Where a period is used, it defaults to 3 months.
sections.why: Likely reason: separate routes let the app fetch each chart on its own. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Three of the routes call a helper on the service through a type escape, so that helper's name must stay in step with them or they fail only when called.

summary: Exposes the analytics routes that feed the health dashboard: the overall dashboard, trends, medication adherence, water intake and risk score.
purpose: Passes each analytics request to the analytics service with the signed-in user and a time period.
why: Likely reason: the dashboard needs several views, and separate routes let the app load each one on its own. The reason for the default of 3 months is not stated.
how: 1) Identify the signed-in user. 2) Read the period, defaulting to 3 months. 3) For the three routes that use a period range, convert the period to dates. 4) Call the analytics service. 5) Return the result inside a data field.
inputs: The signed-in user, an optional period (7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months or 1 year), and the query values for trends.
outputs: A data object for the dashboard, trends, adherence, water intake or risk score.
risks: The period is not checked at runtime, so an unexpected value is passed on unchanged. Three routes call a helper on the service by bypassing type checks, so a rename breaks them only when the route runs.
debug: If a route fails with an error about dates, check the period value sent and the helper it calls in the service. If the dashboard is empty, check the user has readings in that period. The API documentation lists the allowed period values.
